Aim

These maps and distribution plots show the grid-level environmental variables used by the HMSC analysis. The map panels focus on Atlas 1 and Atlas 3, labelled here as the 1970s and 2010s. The violin plots include all three atlas periods so temporal shifts in the land-use distributions are visible.

The map style follows the avian bioregion cluster notebooks: each grid cell is drawn at its model coordinate, with mainland Denmark as the main panel and Bornholm shown as an inset.

Dominant Land-Use Class

Dominance here is calculated only among the land-use predictors retained by the HMSC models: urban, cropland, pasture, forest, and grass/shrubland. The freshwater/saltwater percentage is omitted to match the model formula.

Zero-Inflated Land-Use Distribution View

The plot below separates the two parts of the distribution. The top panels show the percentage of grid cells where each land-use type is present at all. The bottom panels then show the percentage cover distribution only for cells where that land-use type is present. The bottom panels use free y axes because the sparse land-use types otherwise disappear against cropland’s 0-100% range.

Land-Use Relative High-Low Maps

The maps below show whether each grid cell is lower or higher than the same-period distribution for that variable. Values are standardized within each variable x period combination before plotting, so the colours emphasize spatial high-low regions rather than raw units or period-level shifts.

Climate Relative High-Low Maps

These climate panels use the breeding-season temperature and precipitation variables included in the fitted models. As above, colours are relative to each period’s own spatial distribution.
